tecnicas.observacao: Prompt de partida de todas as etapas: docstring em linguagem natural (instrucao) e assinatura do método que fixa nome e parâmetros (restricoes). Parte dos prompts originais do BigCodeBench já traz exemplos de uso e lista de requisitos (p. 6, ID 125; p. 7, ID 553), de modo que exemplos estão presentes só em parte dos prompts; o estudo não quantifica essa parte. Executado 10 vezes por tarefa e modelo apenas para selecionar as tarefas que sempre falharam (Tabela 1, p. 4); não é comparador de eficácia das diretrizes.

tecnicas.nome_original: Code optimization prompt (iterative code optimization based on test failures)
tecnicas.localizador: p. 4 do PDF, seção 3.4 e quadro 'Code optimization prompt'
tecnicas.observacao: Etapa do procedimento de construção do conjunto de dados: o prompt reúne o prompt inicial, o código da rodada anterior e as mensagens de erro dos testes, por até cinco rodadas. Aplicado apenas às tarefas em que o prompt original falhou nas 10 execuções; 229, 261, 268 e 228 instâncias foram otimizadas com sucesso (GPT-4o mini, Llama 3.3, Qwen2.5, DeepSeek). Como a condição sem a técnica é, por construção, a das tarefas que sempre falharam, e a técnica usa informação dos testes, não há contraste em condições comparáveis. Os autores afirmam que o procedimento não se destina a uso prático por desenvolvedores (p. 3).

tecnicas.nome_original: Prompt optimization (LLM asked to produce a new zero-shot prompt Pf from the starting prompt, test errors and test-passing code)
tecnicas.localizador: p. 4-5 do PDF, seção 3.5, quadro 'Prompt optimization' e Listing 2/Figura 2
tecnicas.observacao: O LLM reescreve o prompt original com base nos pares <código, erros> e no código aprovado; o prompt otimizado Pf é executado 10 vezes e considerado bem-sucedido se qualquer execução passar nos testes (153, 192, 200 e 145 instâncias). A validação em 10 execuções é critério de sucesso, não seleção de resposta por prompting, por isso amostragem não foi atribuída. O Pf é produzido com acesso a erros de teste e ao código aprovado, e o prompt original foi selecionado por falhar sempre; o estudo não apresenta essa diferença como medida de eficácia e declara não medir a eficácia das diretrizes (p. 10). Os mecanismos do Pf resultante variam por instância (ver diretrizes da Tabela 2).

Esforço manual: análise de todos os prompts otimizados por pares de autores, com arquivo diff em HTML e log de testes, seguida de consolidação das diretrizes por dois autores.

Os participantes indicaram estratégias não cobertas pelas diretrizes: mais informação contextual (sete respostas), padrões de codificação (duas), requisitos de testabilidade (uma) e aspectos não funcionais (uma).

As contagens da Figura 1 (553, 618, 635, 563 tarefas sempre falhas) coincidem, por cálculo próprio, com as somas da coluna '#Always fail' da Tabela 1 para cada modelo; a Figura 1 indica 1,682 tarefas, número anterior à exclusão de quatro tarefas.

citacoes.trecho: In this work, we derive and evaluate development-specific prompt optimization guidelines.
We use an iterative, test-driven approach to automatically refine code generation prompts, and we analyze the outcome of this process to identify prompt improvement items that lead to test passes.
The goal of this work is to establish guidelines for aiding developers in zero-shot LLM prompting in code generation.
As input to the LLMs, we adopt the prompts provided in the subject datasets (i.e., BigCodeBench, HumanEval+, and MBPP+), which consist of the method signature and its docstring.
Following recent studies [15, 16], we performed the generation process with zero temperature and a fixed seed.
However, since the models do not guarantee full determinism even at low temperatures, we generated ten outputs for each LLM and for each task.
We utilize the LLMs to generate new code based on feedback derived from test failures, until the code passes the tests or a maximum number of optimization attempts have been made.
If the LLM is unable to generate a valid source code within five rounds, the process halts, and the coding task is discarded.
A total of 229, 261, 268, and 228 instances were successfully optimized by GPT-4o mini, Llama 3.3, Qwen2.5, and DeepSeek, respectively, thus progressing to the next step of prompt optimization.
At this point, we instruct each LLM to provide a new zero-shot prompt by learning from the information derived from the code-optimization process.
Based on the above information, provide a new prompt that, differing from the starting prompt, will provide enough details to generate a code snippet that passes the test cases.
citacoes.localizador: p. 5 do PDF, seção 3.5, quadro 'Prompt optimization'

citacoes.trecho: In total, GPT-4o mini, Llama 3.3, Qwen2.5, and DeepSeek succeeded in creating an optimized prompt for 153, 192, 200, and 145 instances, respectively.
We manually inspect all instances for which LLMs were able to generate a test-passing prompt, starting from a test-failing one.
In total, 224/627 of the inspected instances resulted in a conflict (i.e., a different set of optimization guidelines defined by the two inspectors).

We also excluded the second since those contained pieces of information not available in the original task specification, which a developer could only have access to in a test-driven development scenario.

Note that the whole procedure we use to generate Pf is not meant to be an automated process used by developers in practice, since it assumes the availability of test execution results, which are often not available during code generation.

citacoes.trecho: However, there may be several subtle elements that, if missed, may compromise the outcome of LLM-based code generation, such as the explanation of a method/function parameters, return values, pre- and post-conditions, or how exceptional cases are handled.
However, procedural techniques such as CoT inherently require longer prompt sequences, increasing token usage, computational cost, and inference latency.
Moreover, extended interactions have been shown to exacerbate hallucination tendencies in LLMs [13].
Regarding the elicitation, we avoided considering cases in which the LLMs tried to overfit test cases as an improvement pattern.
Regarding the validation, our study does not measure the guideline usage effectiveness or efficacy, nor does it provide exact measures of actual usage.
We mitigated errors and subjectivity in our manual guideline elicitation by having two evaluators for each instance, who reviewed and resolved inconsistent cases.
Concerning the study participants, while their demographics indicate a good diversity in experience and expertise, we cannot exclude a self-selection bias.

Both pre-conditions and post-conditions are among the patterns with a relatively higher frequency of use, with the majority of respondents indicating that they use them at least in 25-50% of the prompts, even though the very frequent use (over 75% of the prompts) is limited to 10% of the respondents.
Postconditions 8% 26% 32% 22% 12%
When we asked participants how frequently they perform prompt improvements, they reported doing it in 25% of their prompts (11), 25-50% (21), 50-75% (12), and over 75% (6).
We kept the questionnaire open for three weeks. Out of about 70 invitations, we collected 50 valid responses.
Also, we plan to conduct controlled experiments to assess the actual guidelines' usefulness.
